name: Gillette Castle State Park
blurb: A stone castle built by a Sherlock Holmes actor, perched over the Connecticut River. Tour the oddball interior, then picnic on the bluff.

name: Thimble Islands Cruise
blurb: A 45-minute boat tour weaving through 100+ tiny pink-granite islands, each with its own story (and a few with mansions).

name: Castle Craig at Hubbard Park
blurb: Short drive or hike up to a 32-foot stone tower with the best panoramic view in central CT. Sunrise here is a rite of passage.

name: Kent Falls State Park
blurb: Connecticut's most photogenic waterfall — a 250-foot cascade with a quarter-mile trail to the top.

name: Mystic Seaport Museum
blurb: A recreated 19th-century seafaring village with tall ships you can board. Easily a full day.

name: Mark Twain House & Museum
blurb: The gloriously weird Gothic mansion where Twain wrote Tom Sawyer and Huck Finn. The servants'-wing tour is the sleeper hit.

name: Elizabeth Park Rose Garden
blurb: America's oldest municipal rose garden — 15,000 bushes peaking in late June. Free, and the Pond House does brunch.

name: Talcott Mountain & Heublein Tower
blurb: A 1.25-mile ridge hike to a 165-foot tower where a hot dog magnate once entertained presidents. Fall foliage jackpot.

name: Devil's Hopyard State Park
blurb: Chapman Falls, potholes 'made by the devil,' and shady hemlock trails. Pairs perfectly with Gillette Castle.

name: Hammonasset Beach State Park
blurb: Two miles of shoreline, a boardwalk, and the Meigs Point Nature Center. The state's beach day, perfected.

name: Essex Steam Train & Riverboat
blurb: Vintage steam train through the river valley, then a riverboat past Gillette Castle. Peak charm, zero effort.

name: Dinosaur State Park
blurb: 500 real Jurassic dinosaur tracks under a geodesic dome. Bring plaster May–Oct and cast your own footprint.

name: Submarine Force Museum & USS Nautilus
blurb: Climb aboard the world's first nuclear submarine. Free, and somehow still a secret.

name: West Cornwall Covered Bridge
blurb: A working 1864 covered bridge over the Housatonic. Pair with lunch in town and a riverside walk.

name: Sleeping Giant State Park
blurb: Hike up the Giant's head to a stone observation tower with Long Island Sound views. The Tower Trail is family-doable.

name: Lake Compounce
blurb: North America's oldest continuously operating amusement park — wooden coaster, lakeside setting, water park included.

name: Yale Peabody Museum
blurb: Reopened after a top-to-bottom renovation and now free forever. The Brontosaurus alone is worth the trip.

name: PEZ Visitor Center
blurb: The world's largest collection of PEZ dispensers, plus a viewing window onto the factory floor. Gloriously niche.

name: Stony Creek Brewery
blurb: Riverside taproom where the kayaks pull right up to the patio. The 21+ anchor for a shoreline day.

name: Wadsworth Falls State Park
blurb: An easy walk to a wide, splashy waterfall — one of the best effort-to-payoff ratios in the state.
